title: The Catholic Document That Rejects Collective Blame

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: The Catholic Church rejects blaming all Jews for Jesus’s death.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: There’s an official document: Nostra aetate, issued in nineteen-sixty-five. Its fourth section directly addresses that collective accusation, instead of leaving it to rumor.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: It says Jesus’s suffering cannot be charged indiscriminately to all Jewish people alive then, or to Jewish people today. It also condemns antisemitism.
scenes.on_screen: CANNOT BE CHARGED TO ALL JEWISH PEOPLE

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: That doesn’t erase the harm the accusation caused. And one declaration didn’t make prejudice disappear. But it matters when someone presents collective blame as Catholic teaching.
scenes.on_screen: COLLECTIVE BLAME IS NOT CATHOLIC DOCTRINE

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: You can discuss religious texts and disagree about theology. That is different from making people guilty because they belong to a community, especially generations later.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: So check what the document actually says, not a comment claiming to speak for an entire faith.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: You don’t inherit guilt from a stranger’s history.
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
